pulse.label: Vladimir Gonzalez gets five years and $119 million. The A's put Aitken's money into their right fielder
pulse.notes: The same cycle Mark Aitken left for Colorado, the A's locked up a player they intend to keep. Vladimir Gonzalez, the A's right fielder, has agreed to a five-year, $119 million contract, $23.8 million a year, avoiding arbitration. It is the biggest raise on the roster this off-season. Gonzalez made $2.7M in 2041, so the new deal adds $21.1M a year, almost exactly the $21.4M that came off the books when Aitken signed with the Rockies. Mike Paulson let a 33-year-old walk on a one-year deal and put the same money into a 27-year-old for five. He earned it. Gonzalez, born in the Dominican Republic, is a 92 overall right fielder coming off the best line of his career: .306 with 161 hits, 28 homeruns, 76 RBI, 17 steals and 4.7 WAR in 527 at bats, with only 60 strikeouts. That 4.7 WAR is more than Aitken's 3.2 and more than any A's hitter this page has written up this off-season. The deal also settles a question Gonzalez raised himself. In C113, with the outfield crowded behind him, he said he was not sure how his clutch performance would affect his chances, that "it's up to Paulson to decide," and named Desmond Morton and Frank Reyna as the players pushing him. He told the young guys, "you can't control what Paulson decides. You just control how you show up," and added, "I earned my spot, sure, but I remember what it was like trying to crack a crowded room." Five years answers who plays right field. It also means Reyna, Morton, JR Rosado and Kevin Clark, whose secondary positions include right field, are competing for left field and the bench.
